package_info.why_malicious: These versions of Log4j2 contain a vulnerability (CVE-2021-44832) that allows attackers with permission to modify the logging configuration file to construct a malicious configuration. By using the JDBC Appender with a data source referencing a JNDI URI, attackers can trigger remote code execution. The vulnerability arises from insufficient protection and filtering of JNDI lookups in JDBC Appender.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when log configuration is loaded or reloaded)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code configures a JDBC Appender with a DataSource referencing a JNDI URI (ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit), causing Log4j2 to perform a JNDI lookup to the attacker's server, which can result in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Referencing external JNDI URIs in log configuration is a known vector for remote code execution, especially when the URI is attacker-controlled.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal log configuration should not reference untrusted or external JNDI URIs, nor should it allow arbitrary code execution via configuration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI DataSources may be used legitimately in trusted, internal environments for database connections, but not with untrusted or external URIs.
key_indicators: External network reference in log configuration
Potential for remote code execution via configuration

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains write access to the Log4j2 configuration file.
Malicious JDBC Appender referencing an attacker-controlled JNDI URI is added to the configuration.
attack_chain.leads_to: JNDI lookup is triggered at runtime.

attack_chain.action: Log4j2 performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker's server, resulting in remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution on the target system.

behavioral_signatures: Log4j2 configuration files containing JNDI URIs (ldap://, rmi://, etc.) in DataSource elements
Unexpected network connections initiated by Java processes to external LDAP/RMI servers
Runtime loading of JDBC Appender with external JNDI references
file_indicators: log4j2.xml or log4j2.properties containing DataSource jndiName with external URI
Configuration files modified to include JDBC Appender with JNDI
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI connections from application servers to untrusted IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Log4j2 configuration files for DataSource elements referencing JNDI URIs, especially those pointing to external or untrusted servers. Detect unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI network traffic from Java applications. Alert on runtime loading of JDBC Appender with JNDI references. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to log4j2.xml or related configuration files.
